about: Which files of the framework repository a public consumer repository (G6-8) may carry as a snapshot, and why. Every file under the roots must match exactly one rule, the first that applies; a file that matches none stops the producer (nothing is public by default). A rule says what the file is for (role), whether it is part of the public set, and which sensitivities it carries (flags: governance = internal engineering or governance narrative; security = reveals how a protection is built or held; thirdParty = contains or lists third-party material; licence = needs a notice). The public set is only what a consumer needs to RUN and VERIFY its project; everything else stays in the private repository.
classesAbout: The purity scan of check:project skips these files (development tools and test material of the first project; industry adapters). The classes are those of the private extraction manifest, which the producer compares file by file; a record carries them as the profile states them.
